message.content:
The title of “best” jazz vocalist is highly subjective and varies depending on personal taste, era, and criteria (vocal technique, influence, innovation, etc.). However, several names frequently appear at the top of lists and are widely regarded as among the greatest:

| Artist | Notable Contributions |
|--------|-----------------------|
| **Billie Holiday** | Pioneered emotional phrasing and storytelling; her recordings from the 1930s‑1940s remain standards. |
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song”; her impeccable diction, scat singing, and pure tone set a benchmark for jazz vocalists. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | Renowned for her rich, operatic voice and wide range; she blended jazz with blues and pop. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | Contemporary artist who blends jazz with folk, blues, and world music; known for her deep, resonant tone. |
| **Diana Krall** | Modern pianist‑vocalist who fuses jazz standards with contemporary pop; praised for her lyrical phrasing. |
| **Nina Simone** | Though often classified as soul/R&B, her jazz roots and powerful, emotive delivery earned her a place among the greats. |
| **John Coltrane** (as a vocalist) | While primarily an instrumentalist, his vocal work on “A Love Supreme” is notable. |

If you’re looking for a definitive “best,” it’s worth exploring recordings from each of these artists and deciding which style resonates most with you.
